BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                          OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI



In the Matter of Union Electric Company             )
d/b/a Ameren Missouri’s Tariffs to Adjust its       )       File No. ER-2026-0291
Revenues for Electric Service.                      )



  APPLICATION TO INTERVENE BY THE CONSUMERS COUNCIL OF MISSOURI


       COMES NOW the Consumers Council of Missouri (“Consumers Council” or

“CCM”), by and through counsel, pursuant to Commission Rule 20 CSR 4240-2.075, and

respectfully applies for intervention as a party in this electric rate case, initiated by Union

Electric Company d/b/a Ameren Missouri (“Ameren Missouri” or “Company”). In support

of this application, Consumers Council states as follows:



       1.     Consumers Council is a nonpartisan, nonprofit corporation that is dedicated

to educating and empowering consumers statewide and to advocating for their interests.

Consumers Council of Missouri was originally founded in 1971 as Utility Consumers

Council of Missouri, and has participated in numerous cases at the Missouri Public

Service Commission, including the previous Ameren Missouri electric rate case.

       2.     Correspondence, communications, orders and the decision in this matter

should be addressed to:

                     John B. Coffman
                     John B. Coffman, LLC
                     871 Tuxedo Blvd.
                     St. Louis, MO 63119-2044
                     Ph: (573) 424-6779
                     E-mail: john@johncoffman.net
        3.    Consumers Council’s interest in this matter relates to the rates, terms and

conditions of service for the Company’s residential electric customers, including low-

income and vulnerable customers. This interest is different than the general public

interest.

       4.    Consumers Council wishes to explore the utility’s proposals further in this

rate case, because the monopoly utility rates imposed in this case could seriously impact

public health and safety. The issues in this case have drawn our attention, and the

organization desires the opportunity to conduct discovery in this matter. Consumers

Council reserves the right to provide the Commission with more detailed positions in this

rate case, following discovery and further review.

       Consumers Council is opposed to any unjust and unreasonable electric revenue

requirement, as well as is opposed to any discriminatory rate design for the utility’s

residential electric customers. Consumers Council is particularly interested in proposing

cost allocation recommendations and conditions that would provide greater assurance

that large load customers are paying their fair share, and that residential electric

customers are not subsidizing power plants or other facilities which are designed to serve

the load of hyperscale data centers.

       With regard to rate design, Consumers Council is generally opposed to the use of

piecemeal surcharges. Consumers Council is generally opposed mandatory time-of-use

rate plans; we prefer that time-of-use rate plans be “opt-in”. Consumers Council also

favors a residential rate design that keeps fixed monthly charges (customer charges) at

a low level, by applying the majority of any necessary rate increase to the usage




                                            2
 components of residential bills, which helps give customers more control over their

electric bills.

       Consumes Council also desires to explore the utility’s proposed low-income

assistance programs, and would like the opportunity to officially submit its own

recommendations regarding how such programs could be structured.

       5.         Consumers Council believes that its intervention and participation in this

proceeding would serve the public interest, and it wishes to become a party to this case

for all purposes.



       WHEREFORE, Consumers Council respectfully requests that the Commission

grant this Application to Intervene, entitling it to fully participate in this proceeding.



                                            Respectfully submitted,

Dated: June 30, 2026                               /s/ John B. Coffman
